reading.body:
This campus publishes 9 MW of IT capacity, the largest disclosed figure in Iowa, though only 2 of 52 mapped data center facilities in the state have revealed their power footprint.

At typical AI training density of 40 kW per rack, 9 MW of IT load suggests roughly 225 racks. This scale suits distributed workloads or smaller training clusters rather than the largest model runs. Iowa's total published data center IT capacity stands at 18 MW across two disclosed facilities, making the state negligible in national AI infrastructure context. This campus represents over half of that small total.

The facility holds certifications for PCI DSS, HIPAA, FISMA, TIA-942, and HITRUST, qualifying it to host regulated workloads in finance, healthcare, and government. The operator's published materials do not name specific tenants. Its 420,000 square feet of technical space indicates a large physical plant, but published specifications omit total campus power draw, PUE, cooling technology, and grid interconnection details needed to assess actual constraints on deployment.

The data does not disclose whether Iowa faces power availability or transmission capacity limits that would constrain further expansion, facts material to whether this facility matters for scaling AI compute. Without information on grid interconnection, announced expansions, or the power footprint of the 50 other facilities in the state, this single number reveals Iowa's current contribution to AI infrastructure but not whether the state is constrained or has spare capacity.
